correctness.rationale: A previously proved unique optimal window set fixes a strongly connected Eulerian overlap digraph. Its exact in/out degrees are 1 or 2; the degree-2 vertices are precisely the 2F_{n-2} words beginning and ending with unequal pairs. All nonbranch outgoing paths append alternating bits, reach a branch within n-1 steps, and cannot form a separate directed cycle. Rooted in-arborescences contract bijectively. BEST has factorial factor 1, and the directed matrix-tree theorem yields the exact cofactor. The verifier checks all critical finite identities n=4..11, full-matrix agreement n=4..9 and direct Euler-circuit counting n=4..7. The proof, not extrapolation, establishes all n>=4.

evidence: Chee et al. (2024) give maximum-length sequence theory for a one-sided run constraint and enumerate necklaces/lengths, not the full number of maximal two-sided no-triple Euler cycles (https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.01454).

The nearest published no-triple capacity theorem gives the length and rigid support, but not the maximizer multiplicity (https://github.com/published-finding corpus/2026/tree/main/2026/11/8/SCOPE-sharp-fibonacci-capacity-and-canonical-window-set-for-doubly-run--aa3ac12cc70f).
broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem counting all optimal cyclic words would dominate this result even without the same determinant. The inspected nearest works either only determine optimal support, or require a different one-sided constraint, so their statements do not imply the exact population claimed here.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior unique-support theorem is a premise, not presented as a new result. Combining that premise with classical BEST yields a generic uncontracted determinant; this work specifically derives an explicit compressed all-order cofactor with a forced-path tree bijection and independent numerical population. The one-sided compressed result does not substitute because the retained windows and degrees are different. Historical original contributions are separated from known premises.

originality.rationale: This claims counting all optimum cyclic no-triple words rather than their previously known maximum length or uniquely forced window set. It gives a two-sided 2F_{n-2}-state compressed arborescence cofactor distinct from the published one-sided Fibonacci no-11 count. Searches and primary-source reading found no prior claim that supplies the same number of optimal tours for this support. Generic tree-counting identities are classical; priority uncertainty for unindexed equivalent calculations remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed older Euler-tour enumerations could be equivalent despite differing vocabulary.

value.rationale: The multiplicity of distinct longest constrained cyclic readout sequences, not simply the optimal capacity, is a natural intrinsic invariant needed to assess how many designs achieve maximum window coverage. A uniform all-length count, compressed determinant, rigid forced-path bijection and nontrivial initial counts advance a previous optimal-length theorem and inform enumeration and randomized generation. It is not a mere substituted known table or an arbitrary slice; no elementary closed product is claimed.
